articles.title: How much is a UFC title worth these days? With PPV gone, the reality is sinking in
articles.summary: UFC champions can no longer dream of pay-per-view riches. Now some, like middleweight titleholder Sean Strickland, seem to be feeling the sting of a harsh ne...
articles.body:
A while back, a reader wrote in with a question for my weekly mailbag that sounded simple but turned out to be trickier than I expected. It went something like this: In the current era, what's the true value of becoming a UFC champion?

In the pay-per-view days, the answer was relatively simple. Every fighter believed that the key to unlocking MMA riches was to fight all the way up the ladder of a given division, win the UFC title, then defend it multiple times. The promotion's standard champion's contract offered every fighter a cut of pay-per-view proceeds, and it was that cut that purportedly made the difference between good money and life-changing money.

Being an especially popular champion also helped, since the share of pay-per-view revenues went up with the event's buy rate, but the belt was the prize that made it all possible. Without that UFC gold, you'd always be just another working fighter, bleeding for your show and win money.

Now UFC pay-per-views are essentially extinct. Fans get every event for the low monthly cost of a Paramount+ subscription. TKO, the UFC's parent company, gets an average of around $1 billion per year just to put on the events . Fighters still dream of UFC gold, but what's that title worth now that the UFC no longer has to share any of that TV money?

It seems like a question worth revisiting now. UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland is clearly unhappy with his compensation. He apparently thinks little enough of the title's value that he's willing to give it up without a fight if it will get him out of his contract and into free agency faster. So what gives? Are those hunks of leather and gold still worth something in the UFC?

I reached out to a few different managers to get some answers. Many didn't want to discuss the topic and most didn't want their name attached, out of concern for how it might affect their relationship with the UFC. But there was a clear consensus on the issue.

For one thing, they said, the dream of pay-per-view riches was already mostly dead even before the UFC ditched that model. Pay-per-views in recent years just weren't selling like they used to. We could all come up with our own list of reasons why — the high and always increasing price of events on ESPN+, the ready availability of alternative means of seeing these events, a general cultural shift away from this relic of the cable TV age — but the result for fighters was the same regardless. Even with the title, they weren't seeing too much in the way of pay-per-view money.

Still, the standard UFC contract already included a bump in pay for becoming a champion, they said. Fighters also get a boost in terms of their "Promotional Guidelines Compliance" payouts — basically the money fighters get to show up to their fight week responsibilities and wear the Venum fight kit the UFC gives them. (Champions get $42,000 per fight under the current system, while challengers get $32,000. Outside of title fights, the pay tops out at $21,000, but that's only for those rare souls with more than 21 UFC fights.)

Managers also said that opportunities to make money outside the cage improved with a UFC title. Champs get more offers for sponsorships, meet-and-greets and seminars. Their supplemental income tends to improve, even if it's not to a life-altering degree.

In other words, yes, it still pays more to be a UFC champion. The difference is more modest than it used to be, several managers said, but it's also more predictable. That has both benefits and drawbacks.

As one manager pointed out, fighters now know exactly what they can expect to make as champion. They aren't chasing some pay-per-view fantasy that may never come true, believing that maybe the next one will top 1 million buys and bring the money raining down from the heavens. Even during the last phase of the pay-per-view era, that was never going to happen for most UFC champs anyway, this manager said. Better for them to discard the illusion altogether and know what they're really getting.

But that knowledge can also be a disappointment. The fact that it is fixed in advance, that no amount of hype or salesmanship or pure athletic performance is going to change that final figure, it can leave some champs feeling stuck. This is the pay and it's not going to get any better, no matter what you do. And if those same champs see reports that TKO is paying other fighters like Conor McGregor or Conor Benn vast sums for a single fight, they might quite reasonably despair at the realization that nothing in their UFC contracts allows them even the remote possibility of reaching that level.

Back in the pay-per-view days, maybe the future still felt like an open promise. A champion's earnings were, at least theoretically, almost limitless. That whole thing UFC executives used to like to say about eating what you kill? That was technically more true then, or at least more possible.

But there's also another consequence to the death of pay-per-view. Now that the UFC doesn't have to worry about selling these individual events, making the case for why each one is worth premium prices, it doesn't have to care quite so much about the overall quality of any given card. That means it also has less incentive to placate any given fighter.

In the past, the UFC might have had more reason to work with a champion like Strickland in search of some compromise that would land him and his drawing power in an upcoming main event. Now? The UFC makes the same amount of money whether he fights or sits at home. And if he sits at home for too long, the promotion can simply take that belt back and let the next two guys on the list fight for the vacant title. Just ask Valentina Shevchenko how easily even a longtime champ can get pushed to the side.

Like it or not, the fact is that those old days are gone and they aren't coming back. UFC champs are living in a new reality. Now they know exactly what to expect. And for many, that is both the good news and the bad.

articles.title: David Mora: "Voy a ir a arrollar"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño está en Georgia para debutar en Rkena este fin de semana
articles.summary: El madrileño está en Georgia para debutar en Rkena este fin de semana
articles.body: Está de vuelta. Ocho meses después, David Mora (10-7) vuelve a la jaula para pelear en la promotora georgiana Rkena. El madrileño del The Black Panther Gym tendrá un combate durísimo ante el azerí Alim Nabiev (4-0) pero vuelve a demostrar que no se arruga ante ningún reto. Desde Tiflis, atiende a MARCA. Pregunta. Ha sorprendido a mucha gente peleando en Rkena… Respuesta. Pues la verdad que estoy muy bien. Sí es cierto que iba a pelear en junio, en mayo… pero se fueron cayendo eventos, no concretaban rivales. Y bueno, al final me concretaron esto a cuatro o cinco semanas y dijimos que para adelante. Estamos en forma, al final yo soy una persona que se mantiene en forma, con lo cual simplemente puntualizar las cosas del rival y ya está. P. ¿Cómo surge esta opción? R. Nos lo propuso Íñigo. Y nos dijo que si queríamos… y dijimos que sí, vamos, no lo dudamos. Con cuatro o cinco semanas, de sobra. Yo a pulir los detalles con el rival que sea, me da igual. Y pues ya está, y aquí estamos. P. Al final, es su trabajo… R. Claro, no, y a mí además me gustan los retos, ¿sabes?. Realmente podría quedarme en casa siempre, peleando en Madrid y cómodamente, con mi pareja, mi familia, estar a gusto, el corte de peso más cómodo… pero bueno, realmente también hay que buscar este tipo de desafío si quieres vivir de esto, realmente. Y yo creo que ahora mismo mi rival, la verdad que es un buen desafío, es un buen rival. Me gusta, me motiva. P. ¿Qué tal el trato con Rkena? R. Muy bien, todo muy profesional, el trato, siempre están preocupados porque estemos bien. Yo vengo desde Madrid, me cubren una semana entera porque no hay vuelos directos. Han pensado realmente en todo, en los peleadores, en su comodidad… y que al final yo creo que están queriendo hacer que la gente de aquí disfrute del show. Están intentando juntar a buenos peleadores, hacer un buen evento y poder seguir haciendo más eventos próximamente. Además que la afición la hay en Georgia. P. Hablemos de su rival: Alim Nabiev. Su 4-0 en MMA es engañoso porque tiene un ‘background’ increíble en ‘kickboxing’. R. Si vemos que tiene más de 70 peleas en kickboxing y K1… entonces es como, bueno, pero a mí me gusta eso, ¿no?. Ver el nivel que tengo de ‘striking’ contra él y sobre todo ir subiendo y mejorando, que yo creo que es el punto de cada peleador. Sentirse más cómodo en la jaula, ir subiendo el nivel con gente que tiene ese nivel o más, que sea mejor que tú. Porque realmente si peleas con gente que sabes que eres superior, realmente no vas a mejorar nada, vas a estar siempre en la zona de confort. Yo creo que esto es una parte buena para mí, para ver realmente qué nivel de ‘striking’ que tengo y desarrollar un juego de MMA completo. Para eso he venido hasta Georgia. P. Es un estilo, el suyo, que además te gusta… R. Creo que mucha gente no se espera lo que va a ver. Después de la última, que sí es verdad que estuve un poco más reservón, digamos… en PFL Madrid quería estar un poco más puntualizando las cosas y puntuando tranquilamente. Y bueno, al final se me dio mal por ese aspecto. Pero en esta directamente voy a ir a arrollar. No voy a esperar, voy a ir a darlo todo al 100% desde el minuto uno. P. Hábleme un poco de sus últimos años: la realidad es que no se han dado los resultados que usted quería. Ha alternado MMA con Bare Knuckle, no ha tenido tanta actividad como hubiera deseado… R. No han sido los mejores años de mi carrera, ¿no?. Pero esto al final no es un sprint, es una carrera de fondo. Realmente siempre va a haber épocas malas, épocas buenas… pero bueno, realmente todo sirve para encontrarse uno mismo. Saber cuál es tu lugar. Seguir trabajando y no ponerte excusas. Yo creo que realmente quien se pone excusas y se rinde es quien lo deja todo. Realmente yo lo dejo todo para seguir invirtiendo en mí. Yo creo que realmente si no tuviese el nivel, no tuviese cualidades para estar en una gran liga y mantenerme, obviamente diría que no sigo con esto. Me dedicaría mejor a dar clases o solo entrenar a los chavales y ya está. Pero yo creo que a largo plazo todavía me queda mucho. Realmente con 31 años todavía soy joven. Todavía me queda mucho por aprender y mucho por enseñar. De lo que sé y de lo que puedo demostrar. Que yo sé que en una jaula muchas veces en 15 minutos no se demuestra todo lo que uno sabe pero gracias a mi equipo, al TBP, seguimos mejorando cada día. Seguimos trabajando. Tenemos nuevos compañeros, los compañeros siguen subiendo. También me exigen a mí subir de nivel porque realmente cuando ellos mejoran yo subo. Esto es lo que te digo, una carrera de fondo, poco a poco. Y aquí el que más cojones le echa, aguanta. P. Ha crecido mucho el The Black Panther Gym… R. Yo no voy a hablar de que es el mejor equipo ni compararnos con otros, pero realmente yo creo que los resultados hablan por sí solos. Entonces, cuando realmente tienes tantos peleadores, ya no solo amateur, profesionales ahora mismo… Lo que te digo, solo con los datos yo creo que hablan por sí solos. Y todavía queda mucho. Seguramente que los próximos peleadores de UFC salgan del TBP. Y te lo digo yo que soy de allí, del TBP. Y te lo puede decir cualquier otra persona que lo vea. P. ¿Cómo han sido estos últimos meses? ¿Ha podido reflexionar sobre el estado de su carrera? Su presente, su futuro… R. Realmente ahora vamos a centrarnos un poco en MMA, vamos a terminar de pulir X detalles en MMA. Porque yo creo que realmente, por ejemplo, nunca muestro ni mi suelo, ni mi lucha. Al final siempre me acabo reduciendo al ‘striking’. Y yo creo que también eso puede ser un problema de realizar también combates en otras disciplinas. Por eso ahora voy a terminar de exprimir todo lo que me queda en MMA. Y después de esta victoria esperemos, pues, tener pronto más fechas. Si salgo bien, yo quiero pelear cada dos o tres meses. Yo no quiero estar en el gimnasio, me aburro mucho. Yo ya que entreno, ya lo hago con una preparación focalizada.

"Poatan" is looking to level up his game going into the fight, and that includes a recent training encounter with two-time UFC heavyweight titleholder Cain Velasquez, who shared footage of their technique training.

articles.title: Ellie Scotney out of first featherweight world championship fight as she withdraws injured from Tiara Brown WBC title clash
articles.summary: Ellie Scotney has pulled out of her WBC featherweight title fight with Tiara Brown; it was due to be Scotney's first fight since her thrilling undisputed title battle in April; Alycia Baumgardner challenges IBF lightweight champion Elif Nur Turhan on November 8 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Scotney had been due box Brown on November 8 but injury has ruled her out of the contest.

It was going to be Scotney's first fight at featherweight after a thrilling battle to beat Mayelli Flores and win the undisputed super-bantamweight championship in April.

Alycia Baumgardner's clash with Elif Nur Turhan for the latter's IBF lightweight world title remains the main event at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, live on Sky Sports .

Ramla Ali's fight with New York's undefeated Mikiah Kreps for the vacant WBO and IBF super-bantamweight world titles is now the chief support.

Mexico's Irma Garcia also takes on Nataly Delgado in an IBF and WBA super-flyweight title unification.

"We're disappointed Ellie Scotney is unable to compete, we wish her a speedy recovery and look forward to seeing her and Tiara Brown back in the ring soon," Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, co-founders of MVP, said.

"Ramla Ali now has the biggest opportunity of her professional career against an undefeated Mikiah Kreps, while Irma Garcia and Nataly Delgado will put their world titles on the line in another major unification bout.

"We're also adding more MVP talent to the preliminary card, including Brittany Sims and newly-signed Shera Mae Patricio competing for a world title, along with undefeated rising star Nat Dove returning for a highly-anticipated rematch.

"Sunday, November 8 is loaded with high-stakes fights featuring some of the best talent in boxing."

Watch Ramla Ali vs Mikiah Kreps on Sunday November 8 live on Sky Sports .

articles.title: El GOAT de la UFC desvela su mayor arrepentimiento: "Pensé que debería haber estado allí"
articles.standfirst: Jon Jones ha confesado que sigue pensando en el UFC Casa Blanca y en cómo la compañía "se olvidó" de él para esa cartelera
articles.summary: Jon Jones ha confesado que sigue pensando en el UFC Casa Blanca y en cómo la compañía "se olvidó" de él para esa cartelera
articles.body: Jon Jones es considerado por la mayoría de amantes y expertos de las MMA el GOAT de la UFC. El peleador estadounidense es doble campeón de la promotora, el campeón más joven de la historia, y su única derrota fue por descalificación por codazos ilegales. Sin embargo, 'Bones' ha desvelado que tiene una espina clavada en su carrera, y es el hecho de no haber formado parte del UFC Casa Blanca. En noviembre de 2024, Jones defendió por primera vez el cinturón de peso pesado de la UFC tras noquear a Stipe Miocic con una patada giratoria. Todo hacía indicar que el peleador estadounidense unificaría los cinturones contra Tom Aspinall -campeón interino en ese momento- en 2025, e incluso el propio Dana White -jefe de la UFC- aseguró que eso sucedería al 100%. La seguridad con la que hablaba White se debía a que Jon había pedido 30 millones y la UFC había decidido cumplir con su parte del trato, pero de manera inesperada se anunció la retirada de Jon después del UFC Bakú de junio de 2025, lo que convertía en campeón indiscutido a Aspinall. 'Bones' les había traicionado y se había echado atrás en el último momento. Sin embargo, el estadounidense quiso volver al enterarse de que la UFC planeaba realizar un evento en la Casa Blanca para 2026 con motivo del 250 Aniversario de la Independencia de los Estados Unidos, aunque la promotora decidió no contar con él para la cartelera más importante de su historia, algo que dolió mucho a 'Bones. El peleador estadounidense publicó infinidad de mensajes y realizó múltiples apariciones públicas presionando para que sucediese, pero finalmente Dana White se vengó de la mejor manera y mantuvo en el retiro a Jones, que en una entrevista reciente con 'The Schmo' ha revelado que este ha sido uno de los mayores arrepentimientos de su vida. "Realmente creo que mi pelea con Stipe fue mi último momento dentro de la jaula. Estuvo la cartelera de la Casa Blanca... una de las pocas noches de mi carrera en las que pensé que debería haber estado allí. Ese fue uno de los grandes arrepentimientos de mi vida. Pero si nunca vuelvo a pelear, creo que estaré jodidamente feliz", sentenció 'Bones'. A sus 39 años todo hace indicar que el peleador estadounidense no volverá a subirse al octágono, ya que tiene muy poco que demostrar y hay pocos rivales que le motiven a su regreso. La única posibilidad es un duelo histórico ante Alex Pereira, pero la situación de ambos no acompaña a que esto suceda, por lo que salvo sorpresa el GOAT de la compañía dijo adiós aquel 17 de noviembre de 2024 sin saber que sería la última vez que pelearía y sin tener una despedida a la altura de su figura.

articles.title: Michael Bisping: What Alex Pereira said about UFC 334 headliner is 'crazy'
articles.summary: The way Michael Bisping sees it, Alex Pereira is probably just salty about his loss to Ciryl Gane.
articles.body:
The way Michael Bisping sees it, Alex Pereira is probably just salty about the UFC 334 main event.

At the top billing of the Nov. 14 card in Madison Square Garden, Ciryl Gane (14-2 MMA, 11-2 UFC) defends his heavyweight title against Josh Hokit (10-0 MMA, 4-0 UFC). In the co-headliner, UFC bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison welcomes the returning Amanda Nunes, who is coming out of retirement.

Pereira (13-4 MMA, 10-3 UFC), who will look to rebound from his stoppage loss to Gane this past June when he meets Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335 on Dec. 12, took aim at the promotion's choice for putting Gane vs. Hokit as the main event.

"Alex Pereira, talking a ton of sh*t, saying that Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit, which is for the undisputed heavyweight title, that should not be the main event in Madison Square Garden at UFC 324, which is just crazy," Bisping said on his YouTube channel . "Saying that it should be the co-main event, that Amanda Nunes vs. Kayla Harrison, which is a phenomenal fight, of course, we all want to see 'The Lioness' back, probably the greatest pound-for-pound female fighter the sport's ever seen, and against Kayla, that'll be a good fight.

"But you don't put that – by the way, they've both been out for a long time. You don't put that over Josh Hokit vs. Ciryl Gane for the heavyweight strap. No, Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit both just fought at the White House, they've got massive names, and it's for the title of the baddest man on the planet, right? That is the main event on any card. Ciryl Gane is the undisputed heavyweight champion of the world, and Alex Pereira is pissed off about it. He's still upset about all the back of the head stuff and whatnot. I'm not even going to get into all that stuff. I've talked about it 20 times. He just needs to let it go because it's not a good look. It really isn't a good look."

Gane is a moderate favorite over Hokit, but Bisping doesn't rule out the rising contender's chances.

"Josh Hokit, he's got to use the wrestling against Ciryl Gane," Bisping said. "It's as simple as that. If he stands on the feet, it's going to be a tough night at the office, but he can mix it up, and he is a really good wrestler, and he's a tremendous athlete. He's a tremendous athlete, NFL, wrestling, MMA, man can seemingly do it all. But anyway, what do you think about all this? What do you think about Alex Pereira going on saying it shouldn't be the main event? That is a crazy shout. That's a main event fight all day long."

articles.title: BFI feud deepens: Secretary General Pramod Kumar alleges intimidation as Rs 40 crore boxing deal takes centre stage
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The battle for control of the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) intensified on Tuesday, with secretary general Pramod Kumar alleging
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The battle for control of the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) intensified on Tuesday, with secretary general Pramod Kumar alleging intimidation of state associations and attempts to derail a proposed no-confidence motion against president Ajay Singh, even as the federation featured in a major Rs 40 crore partnership aimed at strengthening Indian boxing.In letters to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, union sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya and World Boxing (WB) president Gennadiy Golovkin, Kumar sought intervention to protect affiliated state units from alleged threats of suspension and the appointment of ad-hoc committees. Copies of the letters are with TOI.Kumar alleged a breakdown in governance and accused Singh and BFI executive director Col (retd) Arun Malik of using administrative machinery to obstruct the process for moving the no-confidence motion. He claimed that a majority of state units and executive committee members had submitted requisitions seeking a vote on Singh's leadership.The motion is scheduled to be taken up at a special general meeting on Oct 28. Kumar maintained that, as secretary general, he was duty-bound to act on the requisitions and uphold the federation's constitution. He also alleged that his official email access had been revoked without his consent, hampering his work and raising concerns about the security of federation records.Kumar further claimed that state associations backing the motion were facing pressure and threats, and expressed concerns for his personal safety. He urged the authorities to ensure that the federation's records were safeguarded and that the alleged administrative interference stopped.Malik, however, dismissed the allegations as “baseless”. “All these allegations are baseless and not true. We have done no such thing," Malik told PTI.Malik also denied that Kumar’s email access had been revoked. “Nobody has revoked his email access. He can get it checked, we have no issues," he told the newswire agency.The governance row unfolded against the backdrop of a significant push for boxing development, with the National Sports Development Fund (NSDF), Sports Authority of India (SAI) and Indian Oil Corporation signing a memorandum of understanding to support the sport.Under the agreement, Indian Oil will contribute Rs 40 crore over two years towards talent identification, athlete development, coaching, sports science, international exposure, boxing academies and capacity-building for coaches, referees and technical officials.Mandaviya said corporate social responsibility-backed partnerships would play a key role in building a national sports ecosystem, in line with the revamped Khelo India scheme. The MoU signing was attended by senior sports ministry and SAI officials, where Singh and Malik were also present. Singh later interacted with the minister as well.The partnership comes after Indian boxers won six medals, including three gold and three bronze, at the 2026 Asian Games, underlining the need to strengthen the pathway from grassroots talent identification to elite competition.With the Oct 28 vote approaching, the BFI faces a crucial test on two fronts: sustaining investment in the sport while resolving an increasingly bitter internal dispute over its leadership and governance.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chris Billam-Smith: If Jai Opetaia can't fight Deontay Wilder, I will. I've always said I wanted to!
articles.summary: Chris Billam-Smith does not harbour long-term heavyweight ambitions but he would gladly replace Jai Opetaia to face huge-punching Deontay Wilder; watch Billam-Smith fight Cheavon Clarke live on Sky Sports on November 7
articles.body:
Billam-Smith has long wanted to box Australia's Opetaia, who is widely regarded as the best cruiserweight in the world.

But Opetaia is expected to move to heavyweight to fight former world champion Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard before a potential bout with the outstanding cruiserweight David Benavidez next year.

"From what I gather he's going to fight Wilder and then Benavidez," Billam-Smith told Sky Sports .

"Opetaia's fighting Wilder, then Benavidez is his plan and I think he gets beat by Benavidez, before I get the chance to box him and beat him myself."

If that does happen, Billam-Smith would then target Benavidez. "But that's a year away. I'm not going to wait around for a year," he said.

He cannot begrudge Opetaia fighting Wilder - Billam-Smith would do the same himself.

"If Opetaia was to pull out of the Wilder fight, I could fight Wilder," the Bournemouth man said. "We could do it. Who knows what's next, to be honest? I can't look beyond Chev [Clarke on November 7] too much, there's that fear factor there."

Billam-Smith told the Toe2Toe podcast : "I want the biggest fights, the biggest names, not necessarily for belts but if they're for belts, even better. Opetaia hasn't got one of the four main governing body belts but that's a great fight, he's seen as one of the best. That's what I want.

"Wilder, I've always said I wanted to fight him."

Dana White, who promotes Opetaia, told Sky Sports : "Jai Opetaia is more than likely going to be on the undercard. [Wilder] is one that we've been talking about and working on.

"The guy's willing to fight anybody," White said of Opetaia. "It's a very dangerous fight for him considering where he sits in his division right now.

"But he's a fighter; he'll fight anybody, even at heavyweight with a guy who hits as hard as Wilder does."

articles.title: Daniel Cormier Reveals His Side of the Story After Alex Pereira’s UFC 334 Accusations
articles.summary: Daniel Cormier sent a detailed reply to Alex Pereira over claims of propaganda and alleged support for Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit at UFC 334.
articles.body:
Alex Pereira is not holding back his frustration over the UFC's decision to put Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit in a fight for the undisputed heavyweight championship. The two are scheduled to headline UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden on November 14, with the heavyweight title on the line.

Although Pereira is preparing for his own heavyweight clash against Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335, he has questioned how Gane earned another shot at the gold. He has also argued that Amanda Nunes vs. Kayla Harrison would have been a more deserving choice to headline the November event.

Pereira's criticism has not been limited to the matchmaking, either. The former two-division champion recently took aim at Daniel Cormier for supporting the Gane-Hokit matchup, suggesting that the UFC had helped shape the narrative around the fight before officially announcing it.

The Brazilian believes figures such as Cormier helped sell fans on the idea that the matchup made sense for the heavyweight division. While Pereira acknowledged that the promotion ultimately gets to decide its title fights, he was not convinced that public support for the contest developed entirely on its own.

Daniel Cormier Refutes Alex Pereira's Claims With Video Evidence and His Own Explanation

During a recent interview, Pereira claimed about Cormier, "You take Cormier, when I spoke to him, I asked him, 'Hey, this fight, if I become champion against Gane, am I the champion?' He said, 'Well, I don't think so; you have to win', so the guy has some opinions that don't make sense… They're trying to influence people to think that this would be the best fight."

Cormier has finally responded to Pereira's criticism of his alleged support for the Gane vs. Hokit heavyweight title fight at UFC 334. The UFC Hall of Famer addressed the Brazilian's comments on his YouTube channel , admitting he was confused about why Pereira had singled him out.

He began by making it clear that he holds Pereira in high regard but disputed the suggestion that the UFC had asked him to promote Gane vs. Hokit.

He said, "Alex Pereira is one of the best fighters we have seen in a very long time…But today, I was given something by Luis: Pereira did an interview, and he said some things, and I think a lot of it is just a bit confusing to me. One, it's a bout the Josh Hokit-Ciryl Gane fight, but that doesn't necessarily bother me much at all. It's not true, though."

Cormier also denied receiving any instructions from the promotion to build support for the matchup. Instead, he said his opinion came from his own assessment of the heavyweight division.

"I was not told by the UFC to promote this as the fight to happen. I will tell you why I think that was the fight to happen, after some fact-checking….Again, I have nothing against Alex Pereira. If anything, I consider him a buddy of mine. We've had some great moments, we've had some great interviews, we've had some great interactions."

However, the disagreement goes beyond the UFC 334 main event. Pereira also took issue with Cormier's comments about his legacy, claiming the former heavyweight champion told him he would not become the champion even if he had beaten Gane at UFC Freedom 250.

Cormier pushed back on that interpretation, explaining that their conversation was actually about whether Pereira could be considered the greatest of all time. "Guys, that's not what happened. This was before the White House card, and Alex asked me through Plinio Cruz, if he won, would he be the GOAT?"

To clear things up, Cormier played footage of their interaction ahead of the June 14 event, when Pereira faced Gane for the interim heavyweight title. He insisted that his comments had been misunderstood.

"I didn't say he wouldn't be the champ; I said he wouldn't be the GOAT, yet. I'm honest. I don't lie to these guys. I don't sugarcoat to these guys. But I said if he was to win, defend the belt, yeah, we'd have the conversation. But I also said, of course, if he beats Ciryl Gane, he'd be the champion. But I did say that he would be in the conversation. … But I also think that could just be a miscommunication. We don't talk the same language, all those things."

Daniel Cormier Questions Alex Pereira's Claim to an Immediate Rematch With Ciryl Gane

At the heart of Pereira's frustration is his belief that he deserved an immediate rematch with Gane after their controversial encounter at UFC Freedom 250. The Frenchman finished the Brazilian after landing 11 illegal strikes to the back of his head, sparking questions about the circumstances surrounding the result.

Cormier, however, believes Pereira needs a stronger argument for another immediate title shot. While acknowledging the controversy surrounding the illegal strikes, he questioned whether that alone was enough to justify skipping the queue.

He said, "I think he's a bit misguided in how he's approaching it. Because he's trying to get this rematch, and I really don't know what he wants to base this immediate rematch on, outside of possibly the strikes to the back of the head. If he's building his case on, 'I deserve this rematch based on him finishing me in Round 2 with illegal strikes,' maybe. But outside of that one thing, there really isn't much to warrant him getting an immediate title fight."

The UFC veteran also pointed out that Pereira has benefited from opportunities to compete for championships after achieving success at middleweight and light heavyweight. In his view, losing in his heavyweight title debut does not automatically entitle the Brazilian to another shot at the gold.

Cormier even drew a comparison with his own move up to heavyweight. He defeated Stipe Miocic at UFC 226 to become a two-division champion, but argued that things would have been different had he lost that fight. He believes he would not have had a strong case for an immediate rematch either.

For Cormier, the illegal strikes remain Pereira's most compelling argument. Without that controversy, he believes the Brazilian needs to explain why he should get another title opportunity ahead of other contenders.

Daniel Cormier Explains Why Josh Hokit and Alexander Volkov Deserve Title Shots Ahead of Alex Pereira

Cormier also defended the UFC's decision to book Hokit against Gane at UFC 334. Hokit has gone 4-0 in the promotion and picked up wins over Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis, giving him a strong case for the opportunity in Cormier's eyes.

He added that even if Hokit had not received the call, Alexander Volkov would have been a more logical choice because of his history with Gane. That leaves Pereira outside the immediate title picture, at least until he gets another win at heavyweight.

However, Cormier is not ruling out a future title shot for the Brazilian. Pereira is scheduled to face Sergei Pavlovich in the five-round co-main event at UFC 335 , and a victory could put him right back in contention.

He said, "Now, Pereira goes and wins his fight, I would definitely say he deserves to fight the winner. I just don't know that the result at the White House helps him in any way, shape, or form to be fighting for the belt immediately."

Cormier ended his response by reiterating that he has consistently supported Pereira throughout his career. He believes their disagreement may have come down to a misunderstanding rather than any personal animosity, and hopes they can clear the air.

"I just don't want the conversation changing, because now it feels like we are not aligned in terms of our views, when in reality, I have been a big advocate for Alex Pereira at every single step. I just have to chalk this quote up to a miscommunication and a language barrier."

articles.title: Dana White Fires Back at Sean Strickland Over UFC Pay Gripe
articles.summary: UFC president Dana White fired back at UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland over his public pay gripe with the company.Strickland has taken to social me...
articles.body:
UFC president Dana White fired back at UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland over his public pay gripe with the company.

Strickland has taken to social media in recent days to publicly disptue the UFC over his pay, as he feels he deserves to be paid more money now that he's the UFC champion.

White, though, seems to feel differently about things, noting that Strickland signed a new UFC contract in May of this year.

Dana White Fires Back at Sean Strickland

Speaking to reporters after Week 10 of Season 10 of DWCS, White shared his thoughts when asked what he thought about Strickland's public pay dispute.

"I haven't personally (heard what he said); I've just heard through social media and stuff. But when isn't Sean Strickland upset about something or doesn't have something to say?" White said (via MMAFighting.com ).

"Sean Strickland just signed a new contract in May. He just signed a new contract in May. He signed a new deal. Was that like, four months ago? Five months ago? He signed a new deal. And from what I hear, the number he's putting out there, it's not true. The number that he claimed he made is not true."

Will the UFC Give Sean Strickland a Pay Raise?

While Strickland has made it clear that he will not sign a contract to fight top contender Nassourdine Imavov at his current rate, it doesn't sound like White is keen on renegotiating his contract, as once again, the UFC bossman reiterated that Strickland's contract is still rather new, and it's not a situation where he has an old deal that needs updating.

"It is what it is. If we were in a situation where he'd been under the same contract for a year, two years — he just signed a contract in May. He got a whole new deal in May. So it is what it is," White said.

Based on what White is saying, it sure does not sound like Strickland is going to get the pay bump that he desires. But hopefully the two sides can agree to something fair to both parties.

articles.title: MMA Legend Will ‘Bet the House’ on Movsar Evloev at UFC 333
articles.summary: Jorge Masvidal says that he will “bet the house” on Movsar Evloev to beat UFC featherweight champ Alexander Volkanovski at UFC 333.Evloev, who is 20-0 in his...
articles.body:
Jorge Masvidal says that he will "bet the house" on Movsar Evloev to beat UFC featherweight champ Alexander Volkanovski at UFC 333.

Evloev, who is 20-0 in his MMA career and 10-0 in the UFC, is at about even odds to dethrone Volkanovski at UFC 333, which takes place on October 24 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

Masvidal, a teammate of Evloev's at American Top Team, plans on making a big bet on the Russian to win the UFC featherweight title.

Jorge Masvidal Says Movsar Evloev Will Beat Alexander Volkanovski

Speaking on the "Deep Waters" podcast, Masvidal revealed that he will "bet the house" on Evloev to beat Volkanovski at UFC 333.

"He's improved a lot since his last, and not just in his offensive-defensive wrestling and striking, but just overall game as an MMA fighter. You don't know when he's going to take a shot, you don't know when he's going to punch you in the face, his clinch has gotten amazing, too. So, I'm going to have to say it. I'm going to bet the house on him," Masvidal said (via MMAjunkie.com ).

Jorge Masvidal Explains What Makes Movsar Evloev So Good

Masvidal, who has seen Evloev training firsthand at ATT for several years now, has seen massive improvements in his overall MMA game, and he believes the 32-year-old Russian can surprise the 38-year-old Aussie Volkanovski en route to capturing the UFC featherweight championship.

"Movsar, his endurance is so good, and he's so sticky that even when the guys get to their feet, they don't get to break away clean. He's right back in on a shot again. So, he has that double tap button where you're almost away from him, but he'll just re-engage either with a strong body lock or right back into the leg, and just wear on you, wear on you, and get that takedown. I think that's going to happen with Volk. With Movsar's athleticism, too, I don't think Volk is just going to be able to get up and cut free," Masvidal said.

"I think he's going to have a dog fight on his hands every time he gets taken down. … Movsar is one of the strongest guys, period, at 145. It does not fade. His grip, when he goes like this (squeezes), you go, 'Oh man, this guy is so strong,' I'm hoping he fades. No, he stays the exact same the whole way, and that's what I'm really betting on to really wear down Volk with the age, with the wear, the tear on his body already."

While Masvidal is correct to point out that Volkanovski is an older fighter who has been through so many wars during his UFC career, he also has far more experience in championship fights, and that could come into play in this bout.

But in Masvidal's view, getting even-money odds on an undefeated fighter who has been improving rapidly is something he can't pass up, and that's why he plans to bet the house on Evloev to win the belt.

articles.title: No jobs, no visas! WFI prez blasts US embassy after wrestlers rejected: 'India lost out on gold medals'
articles.summary: India’s chances of winning medals at the U23 World Wrestling Championships 2026 in Las Vegas have been affected after nine Indian wrestlers were denied US
articles.body: India’s chances of winning medals at the U23 World Wrestling Championships 2026 in Las Vegas have been affected after nine Indian wrestlers were denied US visas.Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) president Sanjay Singh blamed the US Embassy, saying the wrestlers were rejected because they were under 20 and did not have full-time jobs.Speaking to IANS on Wednesday, Singh said the decision had cost India potential gold medals, with at least two of the wrestlers considered strong contenders. He also pointed out that the issue had never occurred in the tournament’s history."The US Embassy rejected the visas of nine Indian wrestlers on the grounds that they are unemployed. For the first time in history this has happened. Even the UWW president wrote to them regarding the matter," Singh said."This visa refusal is entirely the US Embassy's fault, and as a result, India lost out on gold medals. Among the nine wrestlers denied visas, at least two were strong gold medal prospects. India suffered a major medal loss due to the US Embassy's fault."Men's freestyle team cleared, others affectedAll 10 members of India’s men’s freestyle team received permission to travel to Las Vegas. However, the visa issue affected the country’s Greco-Roman and women’s wrestling teams, leaving nine wrestlers unable to compete.The championships began with Greco-Roman events from October 12 to 14, followed by women’s wrestling from October 14 to 16. The men’s freestyle competitions are scheduled for October 16 to 18.Vishvajit More reaches historic finalDespite the setbacks, India has a chance to win gold through Vishvajit More, who reached the 55kg Greco-Roman final. He became the first Indian to reach a Greco-Roman final at the U23 World Championships in Las Vegas.More defeated Mexico’s Isaac Marin Mata 10-8, then beat U20 world champion Armin Shamsipour 8-1 before overcoming Russia’s Malik Gigiev 7-4 in the semifinals. articles.title: BFI suspends secretary general Pramod Kumar over alleged financial irregularities
articles.summary: The Boxing Federation of India (BFI) has suspended its secretary general Pramod Kumar with immediate effect over alleged financial irregularities, failure
articles.body: The Boxing Federation of India (BFI) has suspended its secretary general Pramod Kumar with immediate effect over alleged financial irregularities, failure to cooperate with investigations and misuse of authority. BFI president Ajay Singh issued the suspension order on Tuesday, pending an inquiry into the allegations against Kumar. These include issuing a work order for broadcasting arrangements without the required approval.Kumar has also been accused of not cooperating with an inquiry into the cancellation of a national championship and trying to call an unauthorised meeting to move a no-confidence motion against Singh."You are hereby placed under interim suspension from the office of Secretary General with immediate effect, pending completion of the inquiry or until the order is modified or revoked by the competent authority, subject to the applicable provisions of the BFI Constitution," read the order, in possession of PTI.The order clarified that the suspension was temporary and "shall not be construed as a final determination of the allegations".Suspension follows Kumar's letter to PM ModiThe action came a day after Kumar wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accusing Singh and BFI Executive Director Col. Arun Malik of "criminal intimidation" to stop the proposed no-confidence motion. Malik dismissed the allegation as "baseless".One of the main issues raised in the suspension order concerns a claim by Pinnacle Broadcast Productions for around Rs 1.5 crore for broadcasting services at the World Boxing Finals Cup in Greater Noida in November 2025.In an earlier letter to the BFI president, Kumar had said Pinnacle had committed Rs 2 crore towards sponsorship and broadcasting for the event. However, the company has denied making such a commitment."The Federation has recently received notices from Pinnacle Broadcast Productions making a claim for Rs. 1.5 crore (approx.) for broadcasting undertaken in the World Boxing Final's Cup, Greater Noida, November 2025."Whereas, the understanding as per the letter forwarded by you to the President was that Pinnacle had committed and assured Rs. 2 crore for the sponsorship and broadcasting of the event.""Pinnacle has now categorically denied making any such commitment, which raises serious doubt as to the authenticity of the letter that you personally represented Pinnacle had issued."The order also alleged that Kumar had signed a work order without getting approval from the federation's finance committee.Inquiry into cancellation of national championshipSingh also referred to an inquiry into the last-minute cancellation of the BFI Elite Men and Women Open Boxing Championship. The event was scheduled to take place in Nahan, Himachal Pradesh, from August 16 to 23.An inquiry committee was formed on August 17 to investigate the cancellation. However, according to the suspension order, Kumar repeatedly sought more time and did not answer the committee's questions."...you have been repeatedly seeking time and have failed to respond to the notice issued to you and the specific questions raised by the duly constituted Inquiry Committee."Dispute over no-confidence motionAnother reason cited for Kumar's suspension was his alleged attempt to issue notices against senior federation officials and call a meeting to move a no-confidence motion against Singh.Last week, Kumar called for a Special General Meeting (SGM) on October 28. He claimed that he had the support of a majority of affiliated state units to move the motion against the BFI president."It is deeply concerning that, instead of cooperating with the ongoing investigations, you have purported to issue cease-and-desist notices against senior officials of the BFI, show cause notices and a notice purporting to convene a meeting to move a no confidence motion against the President," the order read.The order stated that Kumar did not have the authority under the BFI Constitution to issue such notices without the required approval or call special general meetings on his own.It also accused him of sending communications to federation officials and staff asking them to ignore the president's authority and claiming control of the BFI administration."You have also issued communications to the officials and staff of BFI instigating them to disregard the authority of the President of the BFI and claiming to be at the helm of the administration of the BFI."Kumar barred from performing secretary general's dutiesUnder the suspension order, Kumar has been directed not to perform his duties as secretary general, send communications on behalf of the federation or access official records related to the inquiry.The order also warned of further disciplinary action if he attempts to violate the suspension, obstruct the investigation, misuse the federation's authority or interfere with the proceedings."Any attempt to violate the instant order of suspension, obstruct the inquiry, misuse the authority of BFI or interfere with its proceedings shall be viewed seriously and may invite further disciplinary action in accordance with the BFI Constitution and applicable rules and regulations."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: UFC: Aline Pereira misses out on contract after Dana White's Contender Series defeat
articles.summary: Aline Pereira - the sister of former UFC two-division champion Alex - misses out on a UFC contract after losing on Dana White's Contender Series.
articles.body:
Aline Pereira - the sister of former UFC two-division champion Alex - has missed out on a UFC contract after losing on Dana White's Contender Series.

Former kickboxer Pereira was hoping to follow in her brother's footsteps in joining the UFC but suffered a unanimous decision defeat by Sweden's Smilla Sundell.

Pereira, 36, won on the Ronda Rousey v Gina Carano undercard on Netflix in May, but was overwhelmed by Sundell's pressure and volume of punches.

The Brazilian's defeat means she has three wins and three losses on her MMA record since turning professional in 2022.

After the fight, UFC president Dana White said he was unsure about offering 21-year-old Sundell a contract despite her victory because of her inexperience, before being convinced by his team.

"I was scared but I believe everything happens for a reason and I'm really happy it worked out," said Sundell.

Pereira's 39-year-old brother Alex is one of the most successful fighters in UFC history, having won titles at middleweight and light-heavyweight.

In June he attempted to become the first fighter to win a belt in a third division, but lost to heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane.

Elsewhere, White responded to Sean Strickland's claim that UFC fighters are not paid enough by pointing to the middleweight champion signing a new contract in May.

Last week, Strickland said his "heart isn't in MMA any more" and he would prefer a move to boxing because there is "more money to be made".

"When isn't Sean Strickland upset about something or doesn't have something to say?" said White.

"Sean Strickland just signed a new contract in May. It is what it is.

"If we were in a situation where he'd been under the same contract for a year, two years, but he just signed a contract in May."

articles.title: Kayla Harrison Gives UFC Retirement Update in Video Ahead of Amanda Nunes Title Fight
articles.summary: Kayla Harrison doesn't have firm retirement plans following her upcoming fight against Amanda Nunes.
articles.body:
Kayla Harrison doesn't have firm retirement plans following her upcoming fight against Amanda Nunes.

But walking away from UFC also remains a possibility.

"I don't know," she said when asked by insider Ariel Helwani if this will be her last fight. "I don't think so. I don't know, we'll see."

Helwani then suggested it may be a double-retirement fight since "both of you have nothing left to do in the sport. And unless it's a rematch, I feel like you're both done."

Harrison granted it is "a good theory" since "anything is possible" but cleared up her position on her career with potential retirement looming.

"I'm already satisfied with my career," she said. "Let's get that straight. I could walk away tomorrow and be fine and have peace. This is for me. I want Amanda as a worthy opponent. She brings out the best in me. I think I bring out the best in her. It is worth my time and my effort to challenge myself against Amanda. And may the best woman win."

Harrison, who is the reigning UFC bantamweight champion, was initially scheduled to face Amanda Nunes in January. However, the fight was postponed because Harrison required neck surgery due to herniated discs.

Yet they will face each other on Nov. 14 at Madison Square Garden in New York City in a highly anticipated showdown between the champion and Nunes, who is widely considered one of the greatest UFC fighters of all-time despite previously retiring in 2023.

Nunes is a former two-division UFC champion who figures to offer quite the challenge for Harrison.

With such a high-profile showdown looming, Harrison doesn't seem like she will focus on whether she will retire or not until after the fight.

articles.title: Missiles over Riyadh, millions on the line: Canelo Alvarez's next fight faces a crisis unlike any other
articles.summary: Deadly missile attacks have shuttered Riyadh's main airport and forced other major sporting events to change course. But with an estimated $50 million at sta...
articles.body:
On Monday night, residents in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia heard their cell phones ping as official text messages warned of an imminent aerial attack.

It was the third successive day Ansar Allah, the militant organization also known as the Houthis, launched missile attacks targeting the Saudi Arabian capital.

Described by the United States government as a foreign terrorist organization, the Houthis are an Iran-backed political and paramilitary movement from northern Yemen.

The organization said its intention was to strike King Khalid International — an airport that has remained closed since attacks on Oct. 10 and Oct. 11 killed at least 13 people, wounding more than 300.

The airport has been on fire. There has been significant interior damage. At least one commercial aircraft is ruined.

The strikes follow months of escalating hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces, which bombed Sanaa International Airport on July 13 to prevent an Iranian aircraft carrying a Houthi delegation from landing.

Airports throughout Saudi Arabia are "legitimate targets" for continued drone strikes and ballistic missiles, Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a member of the Houthis's political bureau, recently said.

The attacks have placed considerable pressure on Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's economic diversification ambitions. Tourism and sport are pivotal to the country's Vision 2030 program, but Riyadh's principal international airport remains closed, with no confirmed reopening date.

The conflict has already disrupted one of the energy sector's biggest events of the year, with big oil companies modifying their travel plans and event commitments.

BP failed to attend the ongoing WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh, citing "travel disruption" to Reuters . Chief executives from ExxonMobil, Shell, and Chevron were also expected to attend but were absent from Monday's agenda.

The Six Kings Slam tennis tournament, scheduled to take place from Oct. 21–24 as part of Riyadh Season, was pushed Wednesday to take place instead Dec. 27–30. An official statement said the postponement was to do with "logistical reasons."

Only 20 miles from King Khalid International is the Kingdom Arena which, on Oct. 31, is scheduled to host a WBC super middleweight world title fight.

The champion, Christian Mbilli, puts his belt on the line against one of the sport's biggest names and most decorated boxers, Saul "Canelo" Alvarez.

It is Alvarez's first fight since his September 2025 loss by unanimous decision to Terence "Bud" Crawford , against whom he lost his undisputed championship world titles. Against Mbilli, "Canelo" has the chance to win the WBC belt back. An approximate $50 million purse could be his, win or lose.

It is his second fight in the country and one of the year's biggest bouts.

According to one of the principal organizers of the event, Turki Alalshikh, Alvarez "fears nothing" and is said to have reached out to Alalshikh personally to tell him "he'll still fight in Riyadh" on Oct. 31. "Canelo" has yet to speak for himself on the matter.

That determination stands in contrast to safety warnings issued by the U.S. government.

The U.S. Department of State said that, as of Oct. 12, people should "reconsider travel" to places like Riyadh because of the "risk of drone and missile targeting [by] Iranian-supported Houthis."

It went on to say there is a risk of terrorist violence, and that attacks can occur with little to no warning. Targets can even include tourist locations and large gatherings, hotels and locations where U.S. citizens gather, entertainment venues included.

On Oct. 13, the general directorate of Saudi civil defense issued a warning to Riyadh's own residents . Among the instructions was an explicit message to "avoid crowds."

The Kingdom Arena, where "Canelo" and Mbilli are set to fight later this month, seats up to 30,000 spectators.

But with the airport closed, how are "Canelo," Mbilli, their respective teams, fight night officials, and broadcasters supposed to even reach Riyadh?

Once there, what measures are in place to protect them if the Houthis continue their latest offensives?

Combat sports analyst Luke Thomas recently said "trying to force this fight to happen in a f****** war zone" shows the extent of how "broken the sport of boxing is".

Uncrowned contributor John S. Nash on Oct. 11 said Saudi Arabia "is perhaps obsessed with presenting an image of stability" and would rather see this as "a minor hiccup; please keep investing into Saudi Arabia." Nash later added Saudi Arabia might not want to renege on the fight contract because they'd likely be "on the hook for the cost of the event," with "Canelo" possibly "playing a game of chicken" with the state.

Most Valuable Promotions co-founder and CEO, Nakisa Bidarian, shared a similar theory the following day.

"Canelo is due a lot of money," he said. "If he pulls out, he is no longer due that money. If the event is cancelled, he is probably also due that money. Tough situation."

If Alalshikh and other event organizers are engaging in brinkmanship over a $50 million fight, they could keep the date but move the event to Guadalajara, Texas, or Nevada — markets where "Canelo" still sells tickets.

Musical artist Doja Cat has booked the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Oct. 31, but boxing's capital has other venues. MGM Grand Garden Arena and Thomas & Mack Center have concerts the day before but are vacant on fight night, for example.

And though difficult to de-rig a music event, erect a ring, and make it appropriate for an international broadcast production, it is not implausible to turn it around in a 12-hour timeframe. You need only look to Alvarez's own fight history for proof.

Back when "Canelo" fought Jaime Munguia in May 2024, Kwokman Productions documented a 13-hour turnaround to get the T-Mobile Arena boxing-ready following an NHL playoff game the previous evening. Production crews loaded in at 1 a.m. on fight day and successfully prepared the venue for broadcast.

Combat sports is also an industry no stranger to emergency event relocation at the last minute.

In 2018, the UFC relocated its UFC 232 pay-per-view from Las Vegas to Inglewood, California on just six days' notice after headliner Jon Jones returned an abnormal drug-test result ahead of his title defense against Alexander Gustafsson.

Nevada's athletic commission wanted more time to investigate before licensing Jones after a trace amount of Turinabol was detected — a substance he had previously tested positive for prior to a suspension in 2017. California accepted the fight, so the UFC relocated fighters, officials, a production crew, and the pay-per-view operation across state lines during Christmas week.

What remains unclear is whether Saudi Arabia would consider relocating the fight as a practical solution, or an admission it cannot safely host one of boxing's grandest spectacles.

For now, the fight remains scheduled for Riyadh despite the missile attacks, travel warnings, and growing concerns over the safety of all involved.

articles.body:
Former Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) welterweight contender Colby Covington and the always unpredictable Dillon Danis will collide in a submission-only grappling match on Nov. 3 under Hype Fighting in Rome, Italy.

Hype Fighting announced the main event booking Wednesday afternoon via social media. See below:

Covington, 38, has been on an absolute tear since stepping away from UFC almost two years ago. This includes a 5-0 record under the Real American Freestyle (RAF) banner, in which he's become the promotion's Cruiserweight Crossover champion. In fact, Covington already holds a technical fall win over Danis from a meeting at RAF 7 back in March of this year (highlights HERE ). Love him or hate him, "Chaos" has become one of the biggest names in wrestling and grappling over the past 12 months.

Remember, Covington already has a match booked with former UFC middleweight champion Khamzat Chimaev for RAF Abu Dhabi on Nov. 14 (details HERE ).

Danis, on the other hand, is doing his best to stay relevant. Outside of his failed attempt to out-wrestle Covington, the 33-year-old grappler also has a loss to the aforementioned Chimaev back at RAF 10. Danis did capture a win in a MMA exhibition match at Misfits 22 in Aug. 2025, but that came against inexperienced fighter, Warren Spencer. All in all, Danis has struggled to showcase his talents on any stage since his departure from Bellator MMA over seven years ago.

articles.title: AEW Dynamite Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before WrestleDream 2026
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of the final Dynamite before WrestleDream this weekend.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of the final Dynamite before WrestleDream this weekend.

Here's a look at the card AEW advertised for the three-hour special:

Dani Luna and Hyan vs. Britt Baker and Persephone

Triangle of Madness vs. Mercedes Mone and Divine Dominion

Will Ospreay and Andrade El Idolo vs. Tommaso Ciampa and Samoa Joe

Let's take a look at what happened on this week's supersized Dynamite.

The first match of the night saw Jon Moxley, Daniel Garcia and Gabe Kidd take on Wardlow, Mark Davis and Jake Doyle in a trios bout.

While not explicitly babyfaces, The Death Riders were the default fan favorites in this bout due to facing the always villainous DCF. Mox spent more time than usual in the crowd during his entrance to get everyone riled up. The major exception was Wardlow, who got a pop from his hometown crowd.

Garcia kicked things off against Davis, so it was the smallest guy from one team against the biggest guy from the other. Dunkzilla almost laughed at Garcia's attempt to push him at one point.

The most surprising thing about this match was how structured most of it felt. Trios bouts in AEW can often be chaotic, but this one took its time building up to the more exciting stuff.

This might not end up being the match of the night, but it certainly had the crowd invested, especially with AEW being in Wardlow's home of Cleveland, Ohio. It felt like all six guys contributed, but it also felt like it was teasing a possible singles feud between Wardlow and Mox.

Davis ended up pinning Moxley to get the win, which definitely caught a lot of people by surprise.

Result: The Don Callis Family defeated Death Riders

Walker Stewart was with the commentary team this week.

It's going to be interesting to see how this run goes for Wardlow. If he can stay healthy, he could go far.

Moxley testing Wardlow was fun. He looked like he was having a ball.

Marina Shafir taking a shot at Davis was hilarious. The crowd loved it.

The joke of the night goes to Garcia attempting to chokeslam Wardlow.

Another Clockwork Carnage qualifying match was up next with Adam Copeland taking on Josh Alexander, making this the second match in a row with DCF representation.

They started with a simple exchange of headlocks and takedowns. Cope took control for a moment, but Alexander started going after his leg to soften him up.

The Walking Weapon has rarely had a chance to show off in singles competition in AEW, so it was great to see him get the opportunity to remind everyone that he is an accomplished technical wrestler who brings a lot to the table.

This was a decent match, but it felt like it lacked energy in some spots. It wasn't until well after the mid-match break that it started to pick up.

Alexander sent Copeland into an exposed turnbuckle and used his own Spear against him, but it wasn't enough to get the win. Once he recovered, the Rated-R Superstar hit the Spear to get the win.

While Copeland was still in the ring, Don Callis came out with Brian Cage. He told Cope he might not make it to 2027, which led to a few DCF members attacking him from behind. Konosuke Takeshita and the Conglomeration came out to make the save.

Copeland always looks surprised when the crowd keeps singing his entrance music after it stops playing even though it happens pretty much every time he comes out now.

It was a little surprising to see Alexander alone for this bout.

You don't see Copeland hitting a one-legged dropkick too often. It was a nice way to sell his bad leg.

Cage and Takeshita were already in the ring after the last segment, so their match got started right away after a quick video explaining Clockwork Carnage.

Cage had an obvious power advantage, but Takeshita is no slouch. He is a big, strong wrestler who is also quick on his feet, so it felt like this was an even matchup.

The Machine took control after their initial exchange of punches, and he kept the upper hand at ringside by using the environment to his advantage.

This was another Clockwork Carnage qualifier, so it felt like both guys were taking the stake seriously. This was a physical back-and-forth bout that allowed both guys to put their skills on display.

The only real criticism we could have with this bout was that it didn't feel like some of the bigger moments were sold enough. Cage hit a hurricanrana from the top turnbuckle for a near-fall, but Takeshita was back to his feet almost immediately. A couple more seconds of selling would have been easy.

That being said, the pace was good, the action was fun, and we got to see some cool spots from a guy you wouldn't expect to be able to do that kind of offense. Takeshita got the win with a dragon sleeper to advance to WrestleDream.

Copeland gave a speech after his match and revealed Christian Cage was injured at All Out. He put Cage over for finishing the match despite a bad injury. He also revealed 2027 will be his final year in wrestling.

Cage hitting a dive over the top rope will always be cool to watch. You just don't see guys like him do that very often.

Cage hit a 619. It was a little slow, but he still made it look decent.

Tony Schiavone welcomed FTR and Stokely Hathaway to the stage for an interview. They called out The Young Bucks right away, but The Motor City Machine Guns showed up instead. MCMG challenged them to a best-of-five series.

Up next was another Clockwork Carnage qualifier with Okada taking on Reed. This was also an international title bout, so Reed had a huge opportunity to win a belt and earn a shot at another in one fell swoop.

There was a huge difference in the style of these two men. Okada is methodical and technical, while Reed is fast-paced and takes a lot of risks. The nice thing is that both guys are versatile performers who can adapt to other styles.

Whenever Okada was in control, the pace slowed down and he played the heel. Whenever Reed made a comeback, everything got much quicker.

This match probably didn't need to be as long as it was, but the length helped Reed look like a great competitor because he was able to last so long against someone on Okada's level.

Predictably, Okada got the win with a Rainmaker clothesline, but Reed put up a good fight.

Reed's new purple hair really stands out on camera. It's a cool look.

If WWE ever lets Okada have a run with the world title, it needs to lean into how funny he can be.

Reed hit a really nice superkick at one point. The way Okada sold it was perfect.

Triangle of Madness vs. Divine Dominion and Mercedes Mone

Mojo Brookzz, the comedian, joined Kofi, Austin Creed and Prince Nana since Swerve Strickland was unable to be at the show this week. They gave a promo about defending the trios titles at WrestleDream against Hangman and Brodido.

Thekla, Skye Blue and Julia Hart took on Mercedes Mone, Megan Bayne and Lena Kross in trios action ahead of Thekla and Mone's title match this weekend at the PPV.

The CEO and Toxic Spider started for their teams with a fast-paced sequence that led to a stalemate.

This was a solid match with some good action, but it didn't really do much to advance the feud between Thekla and Mone. If anything, the other four women stood out more, which is good for the tag team division.

Thekla was able to get the win by pinning Kross with a stomp, giving her some momentum before her title shot this weekend.

Result: Triangle of Madness defeated Mone and Divine Dominion

There is something special about Kross. AEW needs to make sure she gets a singles push at some point. She could be very popular if booked right.

Thekla has such an expressive face. It really helps her tell a story during matches.

Bayne makes it look like taking a shot from her would be about as fun as getting hit by a car. She lays it in.

The next match saw two WrestleDream singles matches get combined for a tag match when Ospreay and El Idolo battled Joe and Ciampa.

Ciampa teased starting the match against Andrade, but he tagged in Joe before anything happened to play some mind games.

All four of these guys are known for being great in the ring, so saying this match was good almost feels pointless because if you pay attention to the product, you already knew this would be fun before it even happened.

Joe and Ciampa may not be regular allies, but they made for an interesting combination. If AEW insists on keeping The Opps going, adding Ciampa to the group wouldn't be the worst option.

This was a high-energy match that kept the crowd invested after it had already sat through a couple of hours of wrestling. Joe scored the win for his team by choking Andrade out.

Result: Joe and Ciampa defeated Ospreay and El Idolo

Andrade is really taking this ladies man gimmick seriously.

Ospreay's twisting moonsault off Andrade's back was a cool spot.

Ciampa's chops were making some loud impacts.

Joe's walkaway spot is funny every single time.

The next Clockwork Carnage qualifier saw Ricochet take on The Bang Bang Gang's Austin.

These are two guys who can fly with the best of them, but they can also grapple, so their initial exchange was a nice technical sequence.

Austin has been good since coming to AEW, but he has been especially impressive in his last few outings. He might not be getting tons of wins, but he is definitely building credibility as a reliable in-ring performer.

It's actually kind of surprising this was put in the third hour of the show instead of the first because this is the kind of match that would have made the start of the show even more exciting than it was.

There were a little light on selling, but that can sometimes be forgiven when you have two guys who work at breakneck speed like these two. Ricochet ended up getting the win to advance to the match at WrestleDream.

Due to the rules of the match, nobody from their respective groups was allowed at ringside.

The way Ricochet shoved Austin out of the ring was pretty creative. You don't see that kind of thing very often, but it was effective.

The back-and-forth suplex attempts was entertaining, but it also felt a little too contrived.

Persephone and Britt Baker vs. Dani Luna and Hyan

Nick Wayne had a segment in the ring just to celebrate the fact that he beat Chris Jericho. It didn't take long for Jericho to make an appearance. They agreed to one more match at WrestleDream.

The penultimate match on the show was a tag bout with Baker and Persephone taking on Hyan and AEW newcomer Luna.

Hayn came right out of the gate with a running dropkick to take Persephone down after the bell, but it took the TBS champion almost no time to recover and hit a suicide dive.

With Baker being a former champion and Percy being a current champion, they felt like the heavy favorites against two women who are still establishing themselves in AEW.

This bout had good energy, but it definitely felt a little clunky in places. Nothing looked too bad, but there were moments that stood out in the wrong way.

DMD and Persephone ended up colliding when Luna shoved them into each other, and then she rolled up Baker for the upset win. The losers kept up the attack after the match was over, but Queen Aminata showed up with a belt to send them running.

Result: Luna and Hyan defeated Baker and Persephone

Callis, Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight had an interview backstage. The Young Bucks attacked them from behind.

Wayne cutting off Jericho's music to prevent the fans from singing was funny. The song choice for his video package was even funnier.

The Cleveland crowd did not sound happy to see Baker waving her Philly towel around.

Persephone has a presence you can't fake or teach. She feels like a more legitimate fighter than many people on the roster just by how she carries herself.

It was weird that Baker and Luna were not fighting at ringside when the match started.

The main event of the night was another title match and Clockwork Carnage qualifier with Darby Allin defending the TNT title against Hechicero.

Allin tried to use his speed to avoid the technical luchador, but Hechicero eventually grounded him and went after his arm to set up for a submission.

Allin may be known as a risk-taker, but he is also a wrestler who knows how to work against any style. It's easy to forget that he can actually grapple when the main thing people focus on is his huge stunts.

On the same note, Hechicero may be known as a technical wizard, but he can also hit some risky spots when he needs to, so he and Allin were able to combine their styles and deliver a match that felt violent without needing to be bloody.

Depending on the style of wrestling you like best, this might be the match of the night for you. Both guys made sure the fans left satisfied and delivered a great performance.

Allin was able to retain his title and qualify for WrestleDream with two Coffin Drops to get the pin. The Don Callis Family showed up to attack Allin, but United Empire and Copeland made the save.

Hechicero is also the CMLL world champion, but his belt was not on the line tonight.

Walker Stewart was good on commentary, but his voice is somewhat similar to Excalibur's, so it wasn't always clear which one was talking sometimes.

The bump Allin took on the apron looked nasty.

Wednesday's combined Dynamite and Collision special was an action-packed show that also did a good job hyping this weekend's PPV.

Most of the Clockwork Carnage participants were decided on this show, and a few other matches were added to round out Saturday's card, too.

Allin and Hechicero stole the show, but Austin and Ricochet had a great showing, and so did Ospreay and El Idolo against Joe and Ciampa.

However, the most intriguing moment of the night may have been the video that is teasing the debut of Ilja Dragunov. He is going to bring something special to AEW, and anyone who is not familiar with his work is in for a treat.

articles.title: Adam Copeland Announces Retirement Timeline in New Video, Plans to Claim AEW World Title
articles.summary: Adam Copeland will be retiring from professional wrestling.
articles.body:
Adam Copeland will be retiring from professional wrestling.

Copeland announced that 2027 marks his final year as a wrestler on Wednesday's edition of AEW Dynamite while also confirming that he's looking to capture the AEW World Title.

"I'm aging out, and that's okay," Copeland said (0:20 mark). "It happens to everybody. But because of that, I just want to let you all know that 2027 will be my last year in professional wrestling."

"I get it, I get it," he added. "It's time. But all of that being said, that is why I have to go for the AEW Championship."

Copeland also revealed that tag-team partner Christian Cage suffered a collapsed lung and three broken ribs after he was thrown into a ladder at AEW All Out on Sept. 26.

Copeland's 2027 retirement will mark the end of a legendary professional wrestling career that began in 1992, as he started by competing in singles and tag team competitions with several independent promotions.

He finally made his televised debut with the WWF, which was later renamed to WWE, in 1998 as Edge.

During his WWE career, he won 31 total titles. This included 11 world championships. Copeland also had memorable feuds with rivals such as John Cena, Jeff Hardy, Matt Hardy and The Undertaker.

He was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2012.

Copeland eventually returned to WWE from 2020-23 before making his AEW debut in Oct. 2023.

He quickly established himself as a threat upon joining AEW, winning the TNT Championship by defeating Cage at Worlds End in Dec. 2023. It represented the first of two TNT Championship reigns by Copeland.

Copeland and Cage ultimately joined forces, capturing the AEW World Tag Team Championship at Double or Nothing on May 24.

Still, Copeland has yet to win the AEW World Championship.

The 52-year-old will be stepping away from wrestling at the end of 2027, but will attempt to secure the title before doing so.
